findings.message: trigger reads approval from the pushed ref (FETCH_HEAD), but it reads every other gate input from the local working tree. The work-item line in status.md comes from local files, and with --direct the approval is re-read by dispatch's local proposal_approved and the dispatched commit comes from local HEAD. The queued pipeline and the pod read the pushed tree, so trigger's verdict can disagree with the real one. Fix: read status.md (work item id) from FETCH_HEAD too. On --direct, keep the pushed-ref reader (stay check-only for approval) and set F_COMMIT to the FETCH_HEAD commit instead of local HEAD.
findings.scenario: Case 1: run `trigger 049-x --create`. It writes the work-item line into the local status.md only. The user assigns the item and adds fleet:auto, then re-runs `trigger 049-x`. All gates pass and the pipeline is queued (exit 0). The pipeline's dispatch on origin/main finds no work-item line, dies with 'no Azure Boards work item' (exit 1), and the step fails. Case 2: local state.json is still draft (not pulled) while origin/main has it approved. `trigger --direct` passes the gates, then fleet_dispatch dies with 'proposal is not approved'. If local HEAD is unpushed, the pod instead records commit-not-on-ref.

findings.message: FLEET_REF is set from $(Build.SourceBranchName), which is only the last path segment of the branch. trigger queues the pipeline with `--branch ${FLEET_REF:-main}`, and dispatch accepts refs containing '/'. Any slashed branch is therefore cloned under the wrong name. The same defect is in pipelines/dispatch.yml:81. Fix: use $(Build.SourceBranch) with the refs/heads/ prefix stripped.
findings.scenario: Run `FLEET_REF=release/2026 specclaw-fleet trigger 049-x`. The pipeline runs on release/2026 but sets FLEET_REF=2026. The Job runs `git clone --branch 2026`, which fails, and the work item records Failed/clone-failed. For feature/main, the pod clones `main` instead.

findings.message: The run record persisted on the work item names the job, cluster, commit and requester. It does not record which image (FLEET_IMAGE) or which Claude release (F_CLAUDE_VERSION) executed the run. Both decide the outcome, and the self-hosted template's default image is the mutable `specclaw-fleet:latest` (pipelines/dispatch.yml:14). Fix: add image=$F_IMAGE and claude_version=$F_CLAUDE_VERSION to record_run (or to the pod's state=running record). Pin the default image to a tag or digest.
findings.scenario: Two dispatches a week apart both use fleetImage=specclaw-fleet:latest, and the image was rebuilt in between. One run passes and the other fails. The work-item records are identical apart from the job name, so nobody can tell which image or binary produced either result.

findings.message: `only="${only// /}"` removes every space, not just the blank default. A change parameter containing interior spaces can then never match its directory, even though the pipeline test treats space-containing change names as supported. Fix: trim only leading and trailing whitespace. The same line is in dispatch-hosted.yml.
findings.scenario: Running `trigger '050 odd name'` queues change='050 odd name'. The filter becomes '050oddname', nothing is dispatched, the step exits 0, and trigger has already reported ok.

findings.message: The doc says missing consent sets the work item to Failed. In the code, a missing fleet:auto tag exits 3 with nothing written (dispatch.sh, case 10). Only a tag added by someone else, or unreadable history, refuses with exit 4 and Failed. Align the doc with the code.
The egress proxy image is `ubuntu/squid:latest`, which is unpinned. It enforces the security allowlist, so pin it to a version or digest.
check_gates resets `rc=0` and then re-declares `local rc=0` immediately after. This is a redundant leftover; remove one of them.
